run.question: We got a customer complaint about slow response times in Europe. The customer mentioned seeing request ID REQ-EU-8K4M2 in their error page. Find what happened with this request and which service had the issue.

report.summary: Request ID REQ-EU-8K4M2 is traceable to exactly one log document in the searchable log corpus: an ERROR from the auth service in region eu-west, endpoint /api/v2/auth/validate, timestamped 2026-11-18T14:55:47Z, with response_time_ms 15847 (15.847 s) and the message 'Authentication request timeout - request ID REQ-EU-8K4M2 took 15847ms to respond. LDAP backend connection pool exhausted. Customer authentication failed after retry attempts.' (user_id customer-39284). Within the authorized window this is the only ERROR-level document among 1621 documents across all 1620 matched indices (1620 INFO, 1 ERROR), and auth is the only service in the corpus whose response_time_ms departs from the 150 ms baseline every other service and every other auth/eu-west log records. So the slowness in this request is observed on the auth service, and the log attributes it to exhaustion of auth's LDAP backend connection pool. auth itself is not a workload in this cluster (no Deployment, Service or Pod named auth), so its own pod state, resource limits and pool configuration could not be inspected; the LDAP backend is named only as 'LDAP backend' with no host or pool settings visible. Jaeger and Prometheus were both unreachable in this Run, so the request's trace and latency/error-rate metrics could not be checked and no caller-side impact is verified.

claims.text: The only document containing request ID REQ-EU-8K4M2 is in index app-185-geo-eu-west-auth-2024.01.05 at @timestamp 2026-11-18T14:55:47Z: level ERROR, service 'auth', region 'eu-west', endpoint '/api/v2/auth/validate', response_time_ms 15847, message 'Authentication request timeout - request ID REQ-EU-8K4M2 took 15847ms to respond. LDAP backend connection pool exhausted. Customer authentication failed after retry attempts.', user_id customer-39284.

A search over all 1620 matched indices for the authorized window, restricted to level ERROR, returned exactly one document: the auth/eu-west REQ-EU-8K4M2 error at 2026-11-18T14:55:47Z. A whole-window aggregation by service, region and day for level ERROR also returned a single bucket: service 'auth', region 'eu-west', day 2026-11-18.

The whole log corpus in the authorized window contains 1621 documents: 1620 at level INFO and 1 at level ERROR; by service, 'auth' has 61 documents and each of the 26 other services (analytics, api, billing, cache, cart, catalog, checkout, db, inventory, notification, orders, payments, pricing, profiles, promotions, ratings, recommendations, reviews, search, shipping, subscriptions, tracking, users, web, wishlist, worker) has 60.

Comparable baseline for the same service and region: the other 10 auth/eu-west documents (2026-11-14T17:32Z through 2026-11-23T17:32Z) are all level INFO 'Request completed successfully' with response_time_ms 150; only the 2026-11-18T14:55:47Z document carries 15847 ms.

Per-service response_time_ms statistics over the whole window show 'auth' with 61 values, average 407.33 ms and maximum 15847 ms, while every other service shows 60 values with average 150 ms and maximum 150 ms.
The string 'LDAP' matches only that one document in the entire authorized window; no other log line mentions LDAP.

No workload or Service named 'auth' exists in the cluster: the 24 Deployments, 29 Services and 32 Pods returned contain otel-demo services such as ad, cart, checkout, currency, email, flagd, frontend, frontend-proxy, image-provider, payment, product-catalog, quote, recommendation, shipping and valkey-cart, but none named auth. All otel-demo pods are Running and Ready with restartCount 0 and pod start times on 2026-11-23.

The otel-demo fault-injection flag set in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config (demo.flagd.json) contains productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage and imageSlowLoad, every one with defaultVariant 'off'; none of them refers to auth or LDAP.

Log-side evidence for the other services in the same corpus shows no elevated latency: a sampled eu-west catalog document is level INFO 'Request completed successfully' at 150 ms, and no service other than auth exceeds 150 ms maximum across its documents.

An otel-demo feature-flag fault injection (flagd) was considered as the cause of the slow authentication and rejected for the observed state: all flags in otel-demo/flagd-config are at defaultVariant 'off' and none targets auth, and no restarted workload with an unchanged pod template was observed.

The 15847 ms auth response for REQ-EU-8K4M2 was caused by exhaustion of the LDAP backend connection pool that auth uses behind /api/v2/auth/validate in eu-west, as the error text states; the LDAP backend's identity, pool size, timeouts and saturation are not visible in the evidence, so this remains the log's own attribution plus a single correlated latency spike, not an independently observed pool state.

Impact on services the customer actually called (for example frontend or any service that delegates to auth) is plausible but unverified: no trace, span or metric view was obtainable in this Run, and the only observed failure is written by auth itself, so no caller is placed in the affected group.

For human follow-up without changing anything here: retrieve the auth service's own metrics/logs for eu-west around 2026-11-18T14:55:47Z, inspect the LDAP backend connection-pool size, timeout and acquire-wait settings, and check the eu-west caller services for auth timeouts or 5xx in the same minutes.

gaps: Jaeger was unreachable: traces_list_services and traces_search both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so the request-level trace of REQ-EU-8K4M2, its parent-child call path, per-span durations and any caller-side error spans are unknown.

Prometheus was unreachable: get_metric_names returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no latency, error-rate, RPC or Kubernetes metric series (e.g. traces_span_metrics_calls_total, rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket, http_server_request_duration_seconds_count) could be checked for auth, eu-west or any caller; trend statements beyond the log corpus have no metric baseline.

The auth service has no Deployment, Service, Pod, ConfigMap or Secret readable in this cluster, so its pod status, container last termination reason/exit code, resource limits, pool configuration and restart history are unknown; the LDAP backend is named only as 'LDAP backend' with no host, pool size, timeout or saturation evidence.

A Kubernetes events query across all namespaces in the authorized window returned no events (status no_data), so events are not used as evidence here and cannot confirm or exclude a change around 2026-11-18.
The change_history integration is not integrated in this Run, so who or what changed auth or LDAP configuration (and when) is unknown.

Which upstream service the customer was using when the error page appeared, and whether frontend, frontend-proxy or checkout recorded failures for this request, is unverified; no span or caller log supports naming them as affected.
Secrets are unreadable, so any credential or connection-string value behind the LDAP pool could not be verified.
next_steps: Query the auth service's own telemetry (logs, latency histogram, LDAP pool metrics) for region eu-west around 2026-11-18T14:55:47Z to confirm when pool saturation began and how long it lasted.
Review auth's LDAP connection-pool configuration (max connections, acquire timeout, idle/eviction) and compare with the eu-west request rate at that time.
Search eu-west caller services (frontend, frontend-proxy and any service that validates sessions) for auth timeouts or 5xx in the minutes around 14:55Z to establish verified caller impact.
Restore Jaeger and Prometheus access so the trace for REQ-EU-8K4M2 and the service latency/error baselines can be checked instead of relying on a single log line.

The time field is the writer's timestamp, not necessarily when the event happened. total and aggregations cover only the matched indices inside the query window.

Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). <none> means the path reached no value in that object, not that the field is absent from the kind; a filtered table is not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
